question: ‘Mahatma Gandhi National Fellowship’ (‘MGNF’) is a two-year academic programme that was launched by _________in 2020 as part of the SANKALP programme.
solution:
The correct answer is __**IIM Bangalore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Fellowship (MGNF) is a two-year academic programme designed to create a cadre of highly trained individuals for strengthening the decentralised governance in India.
 
• It was launched by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in collaboration with IIM Bangalore in 2020 as part of the SANKALP programme.
 
• MGNF aims to provide academic, experiential, and field training to develop a deeper understanding of the rural economy, decentralised governance, and public policy.
 
• The programme includes a mix of classroom sessions conducted by IIM Bangalore and fieldwork at the district level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE)**

 
 
• MSDE was established in 2014 to focus on enhancing employability and skill development across the country.
 
• The Ministry aims to create a robust ecosystem for skill development through various initiatives and programmes.
 
• It is responsible for coordinating all skill development efforts across the country and aligning them with national standards.
 
 
 
• **Skills Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion (SANKALP)**
 
 
• SANKALP is an initiative of the Indian government to improve short-term skill training qualitatively and quantitatively.
 
• The programme focuses on promoting market-relevant skills, strengthening institutions, and ensuring better access to skill development opportunities.
 
• SANKALP is a World Bank-supported project aimed at transforming the skill development landscape in India.
 
 
 
• **Decentralised Governance**
 
 
• Decentralised governance involves distributing decision-making authority closer to the people, typically through local or regional government structures.
 
• It aims to improve the responsiveness and accountability of public administration.
 
• Decentralisation helps in better addressing local needs and priorities and fosters participatory governance.
